PAPERS.title: Ambient particulate matter and blood lipids: Effect modification by dyslipidemia.
PAPERS.short: KNHANES 2016-2023 province-level annual PM2.5 PM10 blood lipids per IQR dyslipidemia effect modification Korea
PAPERS.pm: Annual PM2.5 and PM10 assigned at province/metropolitan level by survey year
PAPERS.affil: Workers Health Center, Gwangju, South Korea; Chonnam National University Medical School, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Survey-weighted regression in nationally representative KNHANES adults (2016-2023; analytic n not given in the abstract). Per IQR PM2.5 (5.00 ug/m3): total cholesterol +1.17 mg/dL, triglycerides +4.99 mg/dL, non-HDL-C +2.89 mg/dL, HDL-C -1.72 mg/dL; PM10 (IQR 9.00 ug/m3) similar. Diagnosed dyslipidemia modified the association for TC, TG, non-HDL-C and LDL-C; results held after excluding Asian-dust days and extra cardiometabolic adjustment. No CIs are reported in the abstract. The decisive weakness is exposure contrast: one annual value per province-year gives at most a few dozen exposure levels, so between-province confounding (diet, statin use, survey wave) is indistinguishable from PM. Relevance: a lipid shift of this size cannot be resolved with province averages; it is the kind of association that dense sensor-derived residential exposure would sharpen or dissolve.

PAPERS.title: The persistent multidomain health effects of the early-life exposome.
PAPERS.short: HELIX 586 mother-child pairs ~200 prenatal childhood exposures outcome-wide exposome indoor air pollution persisting adolescence
PAPERS.pm: Outdoor air pollutants and indoor air pollution among ~200 prenatal and childhood exposures; PM metrics not itemised in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: 11 outcomes: mental health, cardiometabolic, respiratory, allergic, childhood (6-11) and adolescence (12-18)
PAPERS.affil: ISGlobal, Spain; University Grenoble Alpes, Inserm U1209, France
PAPERS.n: HELIX European pediatric exposome: 586 mother-child pairs, nearly 200 prenatal and childhood exposures (air pollutants, chemicals, lifestyle, built environment) tested against 11 outcomes in four domains at 6-11 and 12-18 years by an outcome-wide, exposure-wide design. A small set of 'master regulator' exposures - maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine disruptors, diet and urban factors - affected several domains, with effects persisting into adolescence; results are released as an open interactive atlas. The abstract gives no PM-specific estimate, so ambient particulate matter is not shown to be among the persistent drivers. With 586 pairs and ~2,200 exposure-outcome tests, power for any single PM association is low and false-discovery control dominates. Relevance: indoor air pollution emerging as a cross-domain driver argues for indoor sensing in child cohorts.

PAPERS.title: Geographic Variation In Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure and Lung Cancer Incidence in the United States.
PAPERS.short: JNCI US county ecological GWR PM2.5 2005-2014 lung cancer incidence 2018-2022 spatial heterogeneity Getis-Ord
PAPERS.pm: County annual average PM2.5 2005-2009 and 2010-2014 (Area Health Resource File)
PAPERS.affil: Boston Medical Center / Boston University, USA; Brigham and Women's Hospital, USA
PAPERS.n: County-level ecological analysis: CDC lung cancer incidence 2018-2022 against AHRF annual PM2.5 for 2005-2009 and 2010-2014, adjusted for poverty, race, education and smoking prevalence. PM2.5 was positively associated with incidence in both windows; geographically weighted regression fitted better than OLS (AICc 20,892 vs 21,810 and 20,883 vs 21,847) and the local PM2.5 coefficients varied across counties. No coefficient magnitude or interval is reported in the abstract. County smoking prevalence cannot adjust for individual smoking history, the dominant lung cancer cause, and GWR local coefficients are notoriously unstable under collinearity; the authors themselves call the map exploratory. Relevance: spatially varying slopes are partly exposure-error artefacts of coarse county surfaces - a testable claim where sensor networks give within-county contrast.

PAPERS.title: Indoor air quality and particulate matter exposure in early childhood centres under natural ventilation and air-conditioned operation in Lampang, Thailand.
PAPERS.short: Lampang Thailand early childhood centres indoor PM2.5 PM10 natural ventilation vs air-conditioning TWA5h dose under-3s
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM2.5 and PM10, 5-h time-weighted averages; inhaled mass and body-weight-normalised dose
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor PM concentration and estimated dose by ventilation mode
PAPERS.affil: Thammasat University, Thailand; Thammasat University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: Eight comparison units in early childhood development centres, non-haze season, children under 3: morning natural ventilation versus afternoon air-conditioned operation, PM2.5 and PM10 converted to 5-h TWA, inhaled mass and weight-normalised dose. PM2.5 was lower under air-conditioning in all eight units, PM10 in seven; CO2 was higher in all eight; PM10 dose exceeded PM2.5 dose everywhere. No concentrations, instrument or sample duration are given in the abstract. Ventilation mode is perfectly confounded with time of day and outdoor measurements were incomplete, as the authors state, so the contrast cannot be assigned to ventilation. Relevance: the classic indoor trade-off (particles down, CO2 up) that combined low-cost PM/CO2 monitors are built to manage in childcare settings.

PAPERS.title: Korean red ginseng (Panax ginseng Meyer) mitigates PM2.5-induced intestinal damage through regulation of inflammatory signaling and gut microbiota.
PAPERS.short: Korean red ginseng mice 12-week PM2.5 intestinal barrier TLR4 NF-kB gut microbiota SCFA protection
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 exposure of mice for 12 weeks (dose, route and source not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Colonic oxidative stress, tight junctions, TLR-4/NF-kB, microbiota, faecal SCFA
PAPERS.affil: Gyeongsang National University, South Korea; Gyeongsang National University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Mice exposed to PM2.5 for 12 weeks with or without oral Korean red ginseng extract (characterised by UPLC-Q-TOF/MS). PM2.5 raised colonic malondialdehyde, depleted glutathione and SOD, reduced ZO-1, occludin and claudin-1, activated TLR-4/NF-kB and disrupted microbiota and faecal short-chain fatty acids; ginseng attenuated each. No PM dose, particle source, route or group size is given in the abstract, so the exposure cannot be placed against ambient levels, and the microbiota-barrier-inflammation links are correlational. A supplement-efficacy design tells little about PM toxicity beyond confirming the gut-barrier phenotype. Relevance: indirect - adds to the gut arm of PM toxicology; no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Respiratory Illness, Weather and Air Pollution in Greater Jakarta During Indonesia's Fire and Haze Season: An Ecological Assessment With National Influenza Forecasting
PAPERS.short: Research Square Jakarta 2026 haze season CAMS PM2.5 ECMWF weather influenza A positivity forecast beta-binomial
PAPERS.pm: CAMS modelled PM2.5 over Jakarta, 92 days
PAPERS.endpoint: National influenza A positivity; respiratory illness context
PAPERS.affil: Vaxcorp Indonesia, Indonesia; Vaxcorp Indonesia, Indonesia
PAPERS.n: Preprint, single author. 92 days (16 Jul-16 Oct 2026) of ECMWF IFS weather and CAMS PM2.5 for Jakarta set against 13 national influenza surveillance reports. Modelled PM2.5 rose from 42.7 to 50.3 ug/m3 between windows - explicitly not station-confirmed - while national influenza A positivity rose from 10.4 % to 60.8 %; a beta-binomial state model projected 72 % (95 % PI 49-89 %) for the week ending 24 Oct. The author states the data cannot support a smoke-attributable burden; the surveillance denominator changed between reports, and national positivity is not Jakarta incidence. Weak inference throughout. Relevance: a fire-haze season analysed with no surface PM data at all - exactly the gap a dense low-cost network around Jakarta would close.

PAPERS.title: Association of Domestic Cooking Fuel Use, Thyroid Function and Complete Blood Count Among Adult Women: A Cross-Sectional Study.
PAPERS.short: Tamale Ghana 100 women cooking fuel LPG charcoal firewood thyroid TSH fT3 WBC neutrophils aOR cross-sectional
PAPERS.pm: Primary cooking fuel type as household air pollution proxy (no PM measured)
PAPERS.endpoint: Thyroid function (TSH, fT3, fT4) and complete blood count
PAPERS.affil: University for Development Studies, Ghana; University for Development Studies, Ghana
PAPERS.n: 100 adult women in two Tamale communities stratified by fuel (LPG/electricity 40, charcoal 27, firewood 33), single venous sample. Crude TSH and fT3 were lowest in firewood users (TSH median 1.15 vs 1.73 mIU/L in LPG; fT3 4.60 vs 5.25 pmol/L) but the thyroid associations vanished after adjustment; higher WBC (aOR 2.49, 1.04-5.96) and neutrophils (aOR 4.17, 1.05-16.57) remained associated with charcoal use. The model is inverted - blood values predict fuel category - so the odds ratios are not exposure effects, and with 27 charcoal users the intervals are wide. No PM was measured. Relevance: fuel type is a crude proxy; kitchen PM sensors would turn this into an exposure-response design.

PAPERS.title: Assessing Organic Aerosol Sources Across PM2.5 and PM10 Size Fractions in Barcelona via Non-Targeted Molecular Characterization
PAPERS.short: Barcelona organic aerosol sources PM2.5 PM10 size fractions non-targeted molecular characterization metadata only
PAPERS.pm: Organic aerosol in PM2.5 and PM10 (from title)
PAPERS.endpoint: Organic aerosol source contributions by size fraction (from title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: Crossref deposit without abstract (Atmospheric Environment). The title indicates non-targeted molecular characterisation of organic aerosol in PM2.5 and PM10 in Barcelona to apportion sources by size fraction. No sample count, period, method or result is recoverable from the record, and no finding is asserted here. Carried because size-resolved organic source apportionment in a southern European city bears on how optical sensors, which respond differently to fine and coarse organic mass, should be corrected. Revisit when the abstract is deposited.

PAPERS.title: Added Value and Geographic Transferability of Same-Day ERA5 Reanalysis for PM2.5 Onset Prediction Across Chinese Cities
PAPERS.short: ERA5 same-day meteorology PM2.5 onset next-day 75 ug/m3 crossing 12+6 Chinese cities logistic average precision transfer
PAPERS.pm: City daily PM2.5; next-day crossing above 75 ug/m3 from non-exceeding days
PAPERS.endpoint: Average precision for PM2.5 onset prediction
PAPERS.affil: Yanbian University, China; Yanbian University, China
PAPERS.n: Additive logistic models predicting next-day PM2.5 crossings above 75 ug/m3 among non-exceeding days in 12 development cities, trained 2016-2021, selected on 2022 and frozen for evaluation to 16 Sep 2026. In 2023-2024 (7,651 city-days, 268 onsets) adding same-day ERA5 surface meteorology raised average precision from 0.307 to 0.358, paired increment 0.050 (95 % calendar-block interval 0.020-0.088); co-pollutant enrichment cut the gain to 0.029, boundary-layer height added nothing, and transfer to six further cities was not established (21 onsets in 2026, opposite-signed increments). Reanalysis is not issuance-time forecast data, so operational value is overstated. Relevance: a sober benchmark - onset prediction from persistence plus local meteorology barely transfers across cities, which argues for local sensor-fed baselines.

PAPERS.title: Lagged associations between climate-related indicators and cancer incidence: a global spatiotemporal analysis.
PAPERS.short: GBD 204 countries 17 climatic indicators 34 cancers Granger causality lag 4-5 years PM2.5 NO2 ozone most frequent
PAPERS.pm: GBD/climate-indicator PM2.5, NO2 and ozone among 17 indicators
PAPERS.endpoint: Incidence of all neoplasms and 34 cancer subtypes 1990-2021
PAPERS.affil: West China Hospital, Sichuan University, China; West China Hospital, Sichuan University, China
PAPERS.n: Cross-correlation and Granger causality between 17 climate-related indicators and incidence of all neoplasms and 34 cancer subtypes across 204 countries, 1990-2021, with meta-analytic pooling and multiple-testing correction. Of 595 indicator-cancer pairs, 105 were significant; air pollution (NO2, PM2.5, ozone) was the most frequently implicated category, with a predominant lag of 4-5 years. No PM-specific magnitude is given in the abstract. Granger causality on smooth national trends is temporal precedence, not causation; both exposure and incidence series are themselves GBD model outputs with shared covariates, and a 4-5 year lag is implausibly short for most solid-tumour latency. Relevance: none for measurement; noted as an example of ecological signal mining that should not be cited as PM-cancer evidence.

PAPERS.title: Greenness, Air Pollution, and Insulin Resistance in a Latin American Megacity: A Longitudinal Mediation Analysis of the ELSA-Brasil Cohort .
PAPERS.short: ELSA-Brasil Sao Paulo 2715 adults NDVI greenness PM2.5 PM10 mediation HOMA-IR insulin resistance 8 years low NSES
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5 and PM10 as mediators of greenness (NDVI quartiles)
PAPERS.affil: Fundacao Oswaldo Cruz, Brazil; Oswaldo Cruz Institute, Fundacao Oswaldo Cruz, Brazil
PAPERS.n: 2,715 non-diabetic ELSA-Brasil participants in Sao Paulo, three waves over ~8 years; mediation of the NDVI-HOMA-IR association by PM10 and PM2.5 with exposure-mediator interaction, stratified by neighbourhood SES. In low-SES areas the top versus bottom greenness quartile lowered HOMA-IR (total effect beta -0.49, -0.91 to -0.05; natural direct -0.59, -1.06 to -0.09), but the natural indirect effect through PM10 or PM2.5 was null. No estimate for PM itself is reported. The exposure source and spatial resolution of PM are not given; within one megacity, a coarse PM surface has too little contrast to carry a mediation path, so a null indirect effect is weakly informative. Relevance: mediation by PM needs neighbourhood-resolved exposure - a natural application for a dense sensor grid.

PAPERS.title: Association of metabolic signatures of air pollution with cholecystitis: a large prospective cohort study.
PAPERS.short: UK Biobank 398697 metabolomic signatures PM2.5 PM10 NO2 NOx LASSO incident cholecystitis HR 1.12-1.19 mediation
PAPERS.pm: Modelled annual PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NOx at baseline residence
PAPERS.affil: Beijing Friendship Hospital, China; Beijing Friendship Hospital, China
PAPERS.n: 398,697 UK Biobank participants with 251 NMR plasma metabolites; pollutant-specific metabolic signatures built by LASSO, Cox models for incident cholecystitis. Higher PM2.5, PM10, NO2, NOx and a composite score were each associated with higher risk (estimates not given in the abstract); the signatures gave HR 1.12-1.19 (all P<0.001; increment and CIs not stated), and mediation proportions ranged 6.05-24.72 %, through albumin, creatinine, VLDL and HDL lipids and omega-3. The signature is trained to predict modelled 2010 exposure from the same blood draw, so it inherits lifestyle and metabolic confounding of the pollutants and its 'mediation' is partly circular. Relevance: none for measurement; UK Biobank exposure is a single LUR snapshot.

PAPERS.title: The ecology of autoimmunity: Influence of pollution on the development of polygenic autoimmune diseases.
PAPERS.short: Narrative review pollution autoimmunity RA SLE systemic sclerosis vasculitis PM2.5 NO2 iBALT citrullination AhR Th17
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident polygenic autoimmune disease, adult and childhood onset
PAPERS.affil: Nationwide Children's Hospital, USA; Nationwide Children's Hospital / Ohio State University, USA
PAPERS.n: Narrative review of pollution and the onset of rheumatoid arthritis, JIA, SLE, systemic sclerosis, inflammatory myopathies, ANCA vasculitis and membranous nephropathy, adult and childhood onset separately. It highlights a nationwide Italian cohort in which PM2.5 above 20 ug/m3 carried 13 % higher autoimmune risk and each 10 ug/m3 PM10 7 % (intervals not quoted in the abstract), and finds associations most consistent for PM2.5 and NO2 in adult RA and SLE; childhood evidence is thin. Mechanisms proposed: inducible bronchus-associated lymphoid tissue, citrullination, AhR-driven Th17 skew. Not systematic, so selection of cohorts is unaudited. Relevance: indirect - autoimmune onset is a long-latency outcome where exposure misclassification from coarse surfaces biases towards the null.

PAPERS.title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Its Attributable Risk Factors in Youth from 1990 to 2021: A Global Burden of Disease Study.
PAPERS.short: GBD 2021 intracerebral haemorrhage youth 15-49 attributable risks ambient PM 14.92 % household solid fuel 14.64 % DALYs
PAPERS.pm: GBD ambient particulate matter pollution and household air pollution from solid fuels
PAPERS.endpoint: ICH incidence, mortality and DALYs, ages 15-49
PAPERS.affil: Dongguan Hospital of TCM, Guangzhou University of Chinese Medicine, China; same, China
PAPERS.n: GBD 2021 secondary analysis of intracerebral haemorrhage in people aged 15-49: 610,000 cases, 260,000 deaths and 13.79 million DALYs in 2021, age-standardised rates falling since 1990 while counts rose. About 79.68 % of age-standardised DALYs were attributable to listed risks; ambient particulate matter accounted for 14.92 % and household solid-fuel air pollution 14.64 %, behind systolic blood pressure (46.59 %) and smoking (21.37 %). Uncertainty intervals are not quoted in the abstract. Attributable fractions are not additive and are entirely determined by GBD's exposure surfaces and IER-type risk curves; repackaging them by age band adds no new data. Relevance: low - burden numbers rest on satellite-fused PM surfaces with thin ground truth in exactly the regions that dominate the youth ICH burden.

PAPERS.title: Global, Regional, and National Burden of Neonatal Encephalopathy due to Birth Asphyxia and Trauma, Its Attributable Risk Factors, 1990-2021: Results from the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021.
PAPERS.short: GBD 2021 neonatal encephalopathy birth asphyxia trauma 204 countries SDI EAPC attributable ambient PM rising household air falling
PAPERS.pm: GBD ambient particulate matter and household air pollution as attributable risks
PAPERS.endpoint: Neonatal encephalopathy (birth asphyxia and trauma) prevalence and deaths 1990-2021
PAPERS.affil: Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, China; same, China
PAPERS.n: GBD 2021 analysis of neonatal encephalopathy due to birth asphyxia and trauma: prevalent cases rose from 446,841 to 508,909 (1990-2021) while deaths fell 31.0 % to 568,255; low-SDI regions gained 112.9 % in cases and Western sub-Saharan Africa 151.7 %. Low birth weight and short gestation led the attributable risks; the attributable share of household solid-fuel air pollution fell while that of ambient particulate matter rose, magnitudes not given in the abstract. PM enters only through GBD's LBW/short-gestation pathway, so it is a modelled risk channel, not an observed association. Relevance: low; records the shift from household to ambient PM in the neonatal burden, a shift driven by GBD's own exposure surfaces.

PAPERS.title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Associated with Particulate Matter-Derived Iron and Magnesium Impairs the Regenerative Potential of Human Upper Airway Stem Cells.
PAPERS.short: Human tonsil and nasal turbinate mesenchymal stem cells PM exposure mitochondrial respiration differentiation ToF-SIMS Fe Mg
PAPERS.pm: Ambient PM (source and dose not stated in abstract); ToF-SIMS mapping of PM-associated metals
PAPERS.endpoint: Viability, mitochondrial respiration, ultrastructure, tri-lineage differentiation
PAPERS.affil: Chungbuk National University, South Korea; Chungbuk National University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: Human tonsil-derived and nasal-turbinate-derived mesenchymal stem cells exposed to PM: cytotoxicity, organelle abnormalities and impaired mitochondrial respiration in both, altered adipogenic, chondrogenic and osteogenic differentiation (TMSCs more susceptible; selective osteogenic suppression in NTSCs). ToF-SIMS located PM-associated Fe+ and Mg+ signals near the cell surface, coinciding with altered mitochondrial morphology; the authors state this does not establish metal-specific mediation. No PM type, concentration or replicate number is given in the abstract, so dose relevance is unknown. Relevance: indirect - upper-airway repair capacity as a PM target; composition (Fe) is what optical sensors cannot see.
